key_insight: Conservative finite-volume discretisation naturally retains the second Brinkman and porosity-gradient viscous terms, improving DBS accuracy without separately discretising them.
engineering_relevance: DBS2 enables accurate flow and permeability prediction directly on voxelised rock images while preserving DBS1’s computational efficiency.
method: Express the full Darcy–Brinkman–Stokes equations in conservative form.
Apply standard central differencing in a finite-volume discretisation.
Implement DBS2 in GeoChemFoam and benchmark against direct numerical simulation.
evidence_signal: Across a microchannel, a 2D heterogeneous micromodel and 3D Bentheimer sandstone, DBS2 reproduced the microchannel DNS velocity field exactly and matched DNS permeability within 1.5–3.8% in the other cases; DBS1 overpredicted permeability by 14.1–37.9%.
watch_item: Validation covers three benchmarks; accuracy for other pore geometries and image resolutions remains to be established.
paper_title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for Digital Rock Flow Simulation with Embedded Second-Brinkman Effects
